notes: Re-parses the raw expression text with ad-hoc regexes on every response instead of using the CEL AST, so it is fragile (unescaped placeholder- or ph()-looking text inside string literals is misclassified as a response condition), duplicates Caddy's expansion logic, and adds per-request regex cost, even though the listed cases and hidden tests pass.

Classifies by running regexes over the raw expression text on every response, which re-implements CEL placeholder expansion, puts parsing in the hot path, and wrongly treats a string literal containing `ph(req, "http.reverse_proxy.status_code")` as a response condition.

AST-based detection is correct, but it hardcodes reverse_proxy placeholder knowledge (plus an unneeded rp. remap and case-folding that misclassifies differently-cased names) into the generic caddyhttp MatchExpression, a layering smell; its tests are thorough, including transport-error retry and direct-ph response retry.

Correct AST-based detection with strong unit and integration tests (including transport-error retries and direct ph calls), but it puts reverse_proxy-specific placeholder knowledge, plus ToLower and rp.-prefix handling, into the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher.

Essentially the reference approach: AST-based placeholder extraction via MatchDescendants/FunctionMatcher, with reverse-proxy-specific classification kept in reverseproxy; minor nit is that Placeholders() returns the internal slice without cloning, and tests cover both the celmatcher API and retry behavior.

Walks the checked CEL AST at provision time to collect literal placeholder names plus a dynamic flag, and keeps the response-placeholder list in reverseproxy, much like the reference; tests cover escaped, look-alike, dynamic and integration cases (Placeholders returns the internal slice uncloned, a minor nit).

Walks the checked CEL AST at provision time to collect literal placeholder names and flags non-literal names as dynamic, then classifies response placeholders in reverseproxy; this matches the reference design, and the tests are broad (shorthand, direct ph, comprehension, escaped literal, similar names, dynamic) plus an end-to-end POST test.

Clean AST walk at provision time with a generic ReferencesPlaceholder(predicate) API that treats dynamic names as possible references, keeps response-specific logic in reverseproxy, and has thorough classification tests including comprehensions and look-alike literals.

Mirrors the reference's prefix handling at every site plus SaveStagedChanges, and the parser follows the spec. The `case renamedTo == "":` switch trick and the long comments are awkward, and parser tests are not visible.

Closely matches the reference: it overrides noprefix, srcPrefix and dstPrefix but leaves mnemonicPrefix alone, and it handles /dev/null, prefixless paths and rename/copy-to lines. The `case renamedTo == ""` inside a tagless switch is a slightly obscure construct, and visible test changes are mainly argv updates.

Matches the reference semantics (forces noprefix/srcPrefix/dstPrefix and leaves mnemonicPrefix alone) and also fixes the SaveStagedChanges pipe. Folding the -c configs into AddCommonDiffArgs is a slightly coupled but effective way to cover every display diff.

Puts the forced prefixes inside AddCommonDiffArgs, a reasonable consolidation that covers every rendered diff (stash included), and keeps mnemonic prefixes. The parser fix is sound, splitting the diff --git line by matching paths, and it adds parser tests alongside the updated argv expectations.

The parser is correct and well tested, including an integration test. However, it forces a/ and b/ with --src-prefix/--dst-prefix, which also overrides the user's mnemonicPrefix display, and it never covers `stash show` (neither the stash entry view nor SaveStagedChanges).

Uses --src-prefix/--dst-prefix flags, which reliably override config, and has a solid parser fix plus thorough unit and integration tests. However, it never applies the forced prefixes to the stash diff commands, leaving a gap in what the task asks for, and it overrides the user's mnemonic display prefixes.

Parser changes match the spec and prefix forcing covers all needed sites, including stash show and SaveStagedChanges. It also sets diff.mnemonicPrefix=false, needlessly changing the prefixes the user sees; parser tests are not visible in the shown diff.

Fixes the parser correctly: any single-component prefix, rename/copy-to fallback, and quoted paths are handled, and prefixes are forced on all relevant diff commands including stash. It also forces diff.mnemonicPrefix=false, which needlessly overrides the user's chosen display prefixes. Visible test changes are mostly argv expectation updates.

Re-aggregates callers from their children after the leaves are cancelled, handles childless callers and emits on settle; the new helper duplicates some cancelOneJob logic, but the tests are thorough (depth 1/2, graceful and force, end-to-end waiter start).

Correct two-pass fix that cancels leaves first and then re-aggregates callers from their children. The new cancelCallerByChildren duplicates cancelOneJob's no-task write path and refreshes a stale in-memory caller. The cancelRun emit also fires whenever no job was updated, which is slightly broader than needed. Tests are excellent: graceful and force cases, depth 1 and 2, and an end-to-end check that the blocked waiter actually starts.

Cleanly makes a task-less caller cancelling while its children are not done and emits the run whenever no job changed (slightly broader than needed), but its tests cover only the nested cascade, not the concurrency-group wakeup.

Minimal fix inside cancelOneJob that writes callers as Cancelling while their children's aggregate is not done. It works but hardcodes Cancelling instead of re-aggregating. On MySQL it may hit the n==0 'changed' error log when the cascade already wrote the same values. The emit fires unconditionally whenever no job updated. The good nested model test is offset by having no test for the concurrency-wake fix.

The caller hook in cancelOneJob keeps the caller cancelling when a direct child is cancelling, and the force-cancel emit is added; but it only checks direct children for exactly StatusCancelling, always reports the reloaded caller as updated, and leaves the old comment saying callers are cancelled directly.

Adds a caller branch in cancelOneJob that refreshes and reloads when any direct child is Cancelling. This works for nested callers via the cascade, but it returns the reloaded caller even when nothing changed, so repeated cancels can trigger spurious notifications. The emit logic is sound, and tests cover the nested handshake plus checkRunConcurrency returning the waiter.

Closest to the reference: it reloads and re-aggregates expanded callers instead of force-writing Cancelled, falls back to cancelOneJob for childless callers, and emits the settled run; the service test only checks that the emit is called.

Closely mirrors the reference. Callers with children are reloaded from the DB and re-aggregated instead of being force-written Cancelled, and unexpanded callers fall back to cancelOneJob. The emit for a settled run fires when no job changed and the run is done. Tests cover the nested-caller handshake and the emit call, but do not exercise the waiter actually starting.

Uses the same exemplar-storage scan as C3 and passes all tests by also clearing `app` and `nextAt` in `truncateChunksBefore` globally. It works, but it is a broader behavioural change, adds an O(exemplar-series) scan per gc, and has a race with exemplars appended after the scan.

Works and passes all hidden tests, but it decides retention from a snapshot of the circular exemplar storage, which means a per-GC scan and a small race window between the snapshot and eviction; clearing the appender inside truncateChunksBefore does cover the ordinary-GC path.

Decides protection by scanning the in-memory exemplar storage before gc, which couples GC to exemplar storage contents and leaves a race window. It also never clears the appender on the ordinary compaction path, so it misses the memory-release requirement (2/3 hidden tests).

Same exemplar-storage lookup design as C1, but series retained in the ordinary gc path keep their appender (and so the removed chunk), which likely explains the failed hidden test; its tests skip appender V2, snapshot and restart-after-recompaction.

Closely mirrors the reference: it tracks a per-series max exemplar timestamp with a has-exemplar flag (so zero and negative timestamps count), protects in both gc paths, releases chunks and the appender with correct metrics, and restores protection on WAL and snapshot replay. Two weaknesses: protection is recorded at commit rather than append time, leaving a small race, and the new head test was inserted under another test's doc comment.

Close to the reference: per-series exemplar timestamp, set at commit and on WAL/snapshot replay, protects the series in both gc paths and releases chunks and the appender; minor nits are recording at commit rather than append, a test inserted under another test's doc comment, and a misleading releaseInOrderChunks comment.

The per-series exemplar tracking is reasonable, but the ordinary gc path keeps the series without clearing its appender, so the persisted chunk stays in memory. Changing the `stripeSeries.gc` signature also breaks the existing callers, and the hidden tests and package suite fail entirely.

Changing the stripeSeries.gc signature breaks existing test callers, so the hidden suite fails to compile; it also never clears the appender for series retained by ordinary head GC, so the last persisted chunk stays in memory.

Closely mirrors the reference semantics, including suffixed root lookup and relying on the local backend for escape protection; the New/NewObject remote-comparison logic and the symlink-only offset hack in zip Open are convoluted, a regular `x.rclonelink` plus symlink `x` produces duplicate names, and the squashfs test needs mksquashfs.

Closest to the reference: zip reads the target lazily from the member, and squashfs uses StatT.LinkTarget with root-at-symlink handled via the suffixed name; squashfs `NewObject`'s double lookup with `exactErr` is clunky, and the squashfs test depends on an external mksquashfs binary.

Well-structured implementation with shadowing checks, docs and strong tests; however, zip members inside a symlink are hidden even without `--links`, and the hostile member is hidden rather than listed as in the reference, so behaviour changes in non-links mode.

Both backends are handled carefully, but `insideSymlink` hides archive members even without `--links`, and directories that share a symlink's name are dropped, which changes behaviour beyond the spec (likely the cause of the hidden-test failure); it also adds docs.

Correct listing and NewObject agreement with good regular-vs-link precedence in either member order and thorough tests; but a root pointing at a symlink only works under the native unsuffixed name, not the listed `.rclonelink` name, and some helpers are clunky (dir `removeLink` is a no-op, link reads are unbounded).

Correct and well tested, including the regular-member-wins collision in either order, but zip targets are read eagerly with an unbounded `ReadAll` that fails the whole mount on error, and root-at-symlink uses the native name rather than the listed `.rclonelink` name.

Nicely shares List/NewObject logic and a link helper in the archiver package, but its aggressive case-insensitive clash filter drops symlinks with members and even hides regular `.rclonelink` files, contradicting the spec that such files stay regular files; it also adds a cross-package helper and heavier refactoring.

Over-engineered: it adds a new shared `LinkFilter` with case-insensitive clash rules that can even drop regular `.rclonelink` members, squashfs `NewObject` rebuilds every entry in the directory on each lookup, and one hidden test fails.

Solid zip and squashfs symlink support with suffix naming, the links notice, root handling and a regular-file-wins rule; however, it drops any symlink that has members inside it (hostile case), whereas the reference still lists it, which likely explains the failed hidden test.

Zip symlink targets are read eagerly with a cap, and an extra clash-resolution pass drops symlinks that have entries under them or share names; this works but goes beyond the spec, and one hidden test fails.

The design that keeps the original listener as keeper is correct in principle and covers double close, races and abstract names, but it adds more machinery (extra dup per socket, logging, restructured types), and all hidden tests and the package suite fail.

A 'keeper' redesign that appears functionally sound (it even handles closing the newest holder first), but it replaces the unixListener/unixConn fields and the unixSockets map type and changes deleteListener to a pointer, so it fails to compile against the hidden tests (0/7).

A minimal fix close to the reference: it closes the leaked dup fd, unlinks via Addr() under unixSocketsMu only on the last close, guards double close with a CAS, and skips abstract names, though its '@' check has no GOOS guard and the double usage-pool decrement remains.

Closely matches the reference: it closes the leaked dup in reuse, drops the leaking File() call in Close, unlinks via Addr() under unixSocketsMu, adds a CAS double-close guard returning net.ErrClosed, and skips '@' names (without a GOOS check), with thorough tests for shared, double-close, unixgram, race and abstract cases.

The keeper-fd redesign with a separate state mutex looks behaviorally sound, and it also fixes double-close of the usage pool, but it changes listenReusable, reuse-time pool accounting and listeners.go, and the hidden tests fail entirely against the new internals.

The broadest refactor: a second mutex, reuseUnixSocket now wraps results and bumps listenerPool, and it edits listeners.go. Locking looks plausibly correct, but it changes unrequested semantics and fails all hidden tests.

The refcounted unixSocket with a keeper fd and release under unixSocketsMu is clean and handles every stated requirement, including closing the newest holder first, but replacing the unixListener/unixConn fields and the map type breaks compatibility and all hidden tests fail.

A shared-state refcount refactor with a held dup fd; it looks correct and includes a GOOS-aware abstract check, but it rewrites internal types and deleteListener semantics, breaking the hidden tests (0/7), and it misses a listenerPool cleanup on its new error path.

On reconnect it restores the configured engine parameters instead of clearing them, so a configured engine ID never gets a fresh discovery; this contradicts the spec and fails a hidden test. It also adds state fields to the wrapper struct and rewrites the production MIB loader, which the issue did not need.

The core close/reconnect flow works, but Reconnect restores a configured engine ID instead of always forcing fresh discovery as the spec requires, and the extra struct fields break positional GosnmpWrapper literals (one hidden test fails); it also includes an unrelated production rewrite of the MIB loader's appendPath.

The SNMP fix is correct and close to the reference, and it includes a good test that a second gather reconnects after a failure. However, it ships an unrelated production change to mib_loader.go (replacing gosmi.AppendPath with AppendFS) just to work around an environment path issue.

The SNMP fix is essentially the reference, with a sensible ContextEngineID reset and good tests, including a check that the next gather reconnects; it is marred by an unrelated production change to mib_loader.go that works around a path-separator environment issue.

Closely matches the reference: it closes immediately on a field or table failure, reconnects in Get/Walk, and resets the v3 engine state and keys. Tests cover v1/v2/v3 reconnects and check that only the failing agent is closed. The only stray change is a test-only gosmi path tweak, and the suite failure appears environmental.

Closely matches the reference with a clean closeConnection helper, and the localized-key reset is harmless; tests check that a healthy agent is not closed and the connection object stays cached, though it needlessly edits the unrelated TestSnmpInitGosmi to work around an environment path issue (the likely cause of the suite failure).

Correct wrapper fix: it resets the USM engine ID, boots, time, localized keys and context engine ID on reconnect, and Get/Walk reconnect first. The deferred close only runs at the end of the agent's gather, so later tables in the same gather still use the stale session. It also includes an unrelated TestSnmpInitGosmi path tweak, and the suite failure looks environmental (gosmi splitting paths that contain a colon).

The wrapper reset (including ContextEngineID) is correct and the tests are strong, even decoding the discovery packet, but the deferred close only takes effect at the end of the agent's gather, so later tables in the same gather do not reconnect; it also includes an unrelated TestSnmpInitGosmi edit.
